      "behind a proxy" profile, because the list depends on the area.
    - **Errors, with the HTTP status from the specification:**
      - a required `_meta` field is missing: -32602, with 400;
      - a version the server does not support: -32022, with 400 and, in `data.supported`, the same list as
        `server/discover` (both eras), by any path; a version from the old era requested in `_meta` also gives
        -32022, with a message saying it only works through `initialize`;
      - an unknown method: -32601, with 404;
      - a header that is missing or differs from the body (`MCP-Protocol-Version`, `Mcp-Method`, `Mcp-Name`, with the
        base64 sentinel): -32020, with 400.
  - **The old era (`2025-11-25`, `2025-06-18`, `2025-03-26`, `2024-11-05`):** keeps using `initialize`, which answers
    with the requested version when it knows it. The server never issues `Mcp-Session-Id`, and GET and DELETE give
    405.
  - **Measured with official clients:** the Python `mcp` SDK 2.3.0, which is v2, in the new era, over stdio and over
    HTTP; and the TypeScript SDKs 1.30.0, the one LibreChat uses, and 1.32.1 in the old era. CI runs all three.

## `kg_query.py`: query and projection over the corpus

Reads many graphs at once and selects nodes, without judging them (the verdict belongs to `kg_validate.py`). Each node
comes out projected: its outgoing and incoming edges, with the other end resolved to its label, local or external,
and whether that end exists in the corpus that was read. With `--root`, the corpus is the `.kg.yaml` and `.kg.json`
files that git tracks under the folder (outside git, all of them under it), and paths come out relative to it, since
it is the root that an external end `<path>#<id>` resolves against.

```bash
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_query.py --root . --open --sort impact          # the open queue
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_query.py --root . --around alvo.kg.yaml#EV_A    # the neighborhood of a node
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_query.py --root . --text "gate base" --type decision --format json
```

Real output in the suite's `external-corpus` folder (trimmed):

```text
alvo.kg.yaml  EV_A  evidence/confirmed/DEV imp=3  A evidência sintética que sustenta A.
    → SUPPORTS Q_A  A pergunta sintética A.
    → REFUTES valid-corpus-external-refutes-refuted.kg.yaml#EV_A  A evidência sintética que sustenta A.
    → REFUTES warn-corpus-external-refutes-live.kg.yaml#EV_A  A evidência sintética que sustenta A.
    ← REFUTES valid-corpus-external-refutes-outgoing.kg.yaml#EV_A  A evidência sintética que sustenta A.
    ← SUPERSEDES valid-corpus-target-exists.kg.yaml (the whole graph)
```

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--root DIR` or files | The corpus. With `--root`, the vendor and the fixtures stay out by default (`vendor/*`, `fixtures/*`, `*/fixtures/*`, `docs/materials/*`, and, since 4.20.0, any folder with the `.kg-ssot-version` stamp); `--exclude GLOB` (repeatable) removes more paths, and `--no-default-excludes` reads everything. A file you name one by one is never excluded |
| `--id`, `--id-prefix`, `--type`, `--status`, `--plane`, `--layer`, `--file` | Filters, all combined with AND |
| `--text WORDS` | Words that the label contains, all of them, case-insensitive; `--in-narrative` also searches the narrative |
| `--open` | The open queue (status `open`) |
| `--verified-before YYYY-MM-DD` | Nodes with no `verified_at`, or verified before the date |
| `--around ID` | The neighborhood: `<path>#<id>`, or an id that is unique in the corpus; `--depth`, `--edge-type` (repeatable), `--direction out\|in\|both` |
| `--sort corpus\|impact` | Corpus order, or declared impact. The attention formula stays with the radar of whoever uses it |
| `--limit N` and `--cursor C` | The page (up to 1000) and the cursor for the next one, valid for the same query over the same corpus |
| `--fields GLOB` | Node keys that come out in `extra`, as they are in the graph: `--fields 'x_*'` |
| `--narrative` | Includes each node's narrative |
| `--format json` | The stable `kg-ssot.query/1` format (`spec/query.schema.json`) |

A graph that does not parse shows up in `unreadable`, with its `parse.*` code, and does not bring the query down. The
label of the other end of each edge is cut at 200 characters: a node with a long label cited by thousands of edges
does not multiply the response. rc 0 when the query ran, even with no node; 2 on broken input. In the MCP server, the
same query is the `kg_query` tool, over the store: the page stops at the server's byte cap (with at least one node),
and `next_cursor` picks up where it stopped. Each call rereads and reparses the area's store, and in a store of tens
of MB the first call takes tens of seconds; the judgment cache comes in 4.19.

## `kg_diff.py`: diff by id between revisions

Compares two graphs, or every graph that changed between two git revisions, aligning nodes by id and edges by their
ends and type. Whatever exists on only one side was added or removed, and whatever exists on both sides comes out with
each field that changed, before and after. Node order in the file does not count; an id change is a removal plus an
addition; a list inside a node is compared as a whole; an edge that changes type with the same ends comes out as an
`edge_type` change. The revision is read with `git show`, with no checkout. It is not a patch: the diff informs, it
does not apply.

```bash
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_diff.py notice.kg.yaml erratum.kg.yaml
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_diff.py HEAD~1:docs/x.kg.yaml HEAD:docs/x.kg.yaml
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_diff.py --from origin/main --ignore verified_at      # everything that changed on the branch
```

Real output, between two suite cases:

```text
valid-node-touched-only-as-target.kg.yaml (modified)
  ~ meta.id: valid-chain → valid-node-touched-only-as-target
  + C_ALVO  Nó sintético C_ALVO.
  - C_B  Nó sintético C_B.
  + edge EV_A -SUPPORTS-> C_ALVO
  - edge C_B -SUPPORTS-> EV_A
· 1 graph(s): 1 modified, 0 added, 0 removed, 0 unreadable; nodes +1 -1 ~0; edges +1 -1 ~0
```

A field that leaves one path and enters another with the same value, in a node, an edge, or the meta, shows up as a
rename (`x_location → x_storage (renamed)`) when the value is not trivial and is unique on both sides. In the JSON,
both entries stay, each with the value at its own path, linked by `renamed_to` and `renamed_from`; the human text and
the per-field summary show a single line. With `--from` and no paths, the vendor and the fixtures stay out (also a
`fixtures/` folder at the root, and, since 4.20.0, any folder with the `.kg-ssot-version` stamp on either side), as in
`kg_query`: a vendor update changes the suite fixtures by the hundreds.
`--exclude` and `--no-default-excludes` work the same way. The meta comes out together with the other root keys,
values are compared in the contract's JSON form, a renamed file comes out as a removal plus an addition, and without
`--to` (or with `--to WORKTREE`, since 4.20.0) the working tree is the after side, and the new graphs not yet added to
git come in too. `WORKTREE:PATH` reads the working-tree file, from the repository root like `REV:PATH` and never
outside it (git's `./` and `../`, relative to the current directory, do not apply), to review an edit before the
commit
(`HEAD:docs/x.kg.yaml WORKTREE:docs/x.kg.yaml`); a branch named `WORKTREE` is read as `refs/heads/WORKTREE`. A
side that cannot be read (not UTF-8, or does not parse) shows up in `unreadable` and counts as a difference; a
revision that starts with `-` is broken input. In an argument, a path that exists on disk wins over a `REV:PATH` read.

`--ignore FIELD` (repeatable) removes a field from the comparison, together with everything below it (`provenance`
removes all three; in the meta, `meta.date`): a `verified_at` that a generator restamps on every run hides the signal,
and the summary counts nodes per changed field to show it. `--format json` gives `kg-ssot.diff/1`
(`spec/diff.schema.json`). rc 0 with no difference, 1 with a difference, 2 on broken input.

## `kg_vocab.py`: the domain vocabulary

Reads the terms of the `x_term` profile (chapter 3) from a corpus, with `--root` or the files, and does three things:
lists them, resolves a text to its term, and exports them.

```bash
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_vocab.py terms --root . --as-of 2027-05-01      # terms, synonyms, what is due
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_vocab.py lookup "codigo de barras" --root .     # the term behind a text
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_vocab.py lookup "cod barras" --case "edital 12" --root .
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_vocab.py export --to skos --root . > vocab.ttl
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_vocab.py export --to ossie --root . > vocab.ossie.json
```

- **`lookup` compares without case, accents, or repeated spaces.** It matches the preferred term or a synonym. A
  synonym scoped to a case only matches with `--case` set to that case. A retired synonym still matches, marked as
  retired, and a superseded term comes with the terms that replace it. rc 1 when nothing matches.
- **`terms` shows when each synonym is due** (`verified_at` plus `reverify_every`, on the `--as-of` date, today by
  default). A retired synonym is never due.
- **`export --to skos`** writes Turtle in SKOS-XL with the ISO 25964 names (iso-thes). The concept gets
  `skos:prefLabel`, plus `skos:altLabel` and `skos:hiddenLabel` for the current domain synonyms, so a plain SKOS reader
  sees them. Each label becomes an `skosxl:Label` with its literal form and its provenance (`dc:source`, `kg:locator`,
  `kg:sourceVersion`, `kg:verifiedAt`, `kg:reverifyEvery`). A case-scoped synonym is linked by `kg:caseLabel`, with
  `kg:scope` and `kg:case`, and not by `skosxl:altLabel`, which would imply an `skos:altLabel` valid for the whole
  concept. A scope that cannot be read counts as a case that never matches. A retired one goes as `isothes:status "retired"`
  and an `skos:historyNote`. A synonym that repeats a literal already said in the concept goes by `kg:repeatedLabel`, so the concept
  never has the same label twice. A superseded term gets `dct:isReplacedBy`. The concept IRI is `<base><meta.id>#<id>`, the
  same one `kg_prov_export.py` gives the node (`--base`, `urn:kg-ssot:graph:` by default); without `meta.id`, the
  relative path given, or the file name, never an absolute path.
- **`export --to ossie`** writes one item per live term for [Apache Ossie](https://github.com/open-semantic-interchange/OSI):
  `name` (the preferred term), `description`, `ai_context.synonyms` (the current domain synonyms), and a
  `custom_extensions` entry from `KG_SSOT` with the provenance of each synonym, because Ossie has no field for it. You
  merge each item into the entity of your semantic model (dataset, field, or metric) by name.
- With `--format json`, `terms` and `lookup` use the `kg-ssot.vocab/1` format (`spec/vocab.schema.json`). The tool does
  not judge: an `x_term` outside the profile is read as far as it can be, and the SHOULD flags the rest.

## `kg_criterion.py`: the pre-registered criterion (4.21.0)

The reader already warns, between nodes of the same graph, about a criterion that is not there, a cited `sha256` that
is not the one of the version, and a result measured after seeing the data (chapter 3, `x_criterion` and
`x_measured_under`). It computes no hash and reads no corpus, so that a JavaScript reader stays free of crypto. This
tool does the rest, from the repository root:

```bash
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_criterion.py digest --text "Passes with 9 of 10 replicas."
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_criterion.py digest --ref criteria/a7.tsv                  # the whole file
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_criterion.py digest --ref data/judge-verdicts.json#CU1      # one list item
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_criterion.py check --root .
```

- **`digest`** prints the `sha256` to write in `x_criterion`. The forms:
  - `text`: UTF-8, with CRLF and a lone CR turned into LF, and without the space (U+0020) at the end of each line. A
    tab stays.
  - `ref` without a fragment: the bytes of the file with CRLF turned into LF, and nothing else. A TSV keeps its empty
    columns, with a tab at the end of the line.
  - `ref` with a fragment: the item in the canonical JCS form ([RFC 8785](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8785)),
    from a `.json`, `.yaml`, or `.yml` file. The fragment is a JSON Pointer (`#/criteria/0`) or the `id` of a list
    item (`#CU1`), unique in the file.
- **`check`** checks every `x_criterion` with exactly one of `ref` and `text` against it:
  - `integrity.criterion-digest` when the `sha256` does not match;
  - `integrity.criterion-ref-unreadable` when the file, the fragment, or a value does not read: a JSON NaN, an integer
    beyond ±(2^53−1), a repeated key, a YAML map key that is not text, or a path that is not a regular file or is
    larger than 64 MiB;
  - `integrity.criterion-malformed` when the version cannot be checked: the `sha256` is not text (a hash of digits
    alone, without quotes, reads as a number), or there is not exactly one of `ref` and `text`, in text. An
    `x_measured_under` that is not a map with a list of citation maps, and a citation of another graph whose `sha256`
    is not text (even when that graph was not given), come out the same way. Since 4.21.1; before, the check skipped
    them.
- **Citations of another graph.** `check` also follows each `<path>#<id>` citation in an `x_measured_under`, with the
  same rule as the reader: `integrity.criterion-unknown`, `integrity.criterion-sha-mismatch`,
  `integrity.measured-post-hoc`, and `integrity.measured-order-unknown`.
- **What it reads.** With `--root` alone, `check` reads the graphs git tracks under it, without the vendor. With files,
  it reads only those, each by its path relative to `--root` (the current folder without it), which is also where each
  `ref` starts, so `g/a.kg.yaml#C1` finds the file however it was typed; a citation of a graph that was not given is
  counted as unchecked, not as a finding, and a given `--exclude` applies to the files too.
- **Paths.** A `ref` cannot leave the root. The last `#` splits the path from the fragment, and an empty fragment
  (`a.json#`) is the whole document. A `.yaml` file needs a map at its root. A byte-order mark at the start of
  `--text-file` is not part of the text.
- **Output and rc.** `--format json` gives `kg-ssot.criterion/1` (`spec/criterion.schema.json`). rc 0 with no
  finding, 1 with a finding or a graph that does not read, and 2 on broken input.
- **What it does not check.** `check` checks that each version matches its text today, not its history: editing a
  criterion in place and writing the new `sha256` passes, and only a result that cites the old `sha256` shows it. Review
  a changed `x_criterion.sha256` in `kg_diff` (it shows as a changed field of the node): a new rule is an amendment, a
  new node with `amends`.
- **In CI.** The reader does not hash, so a criterion edited in place without a new `sha256` is caught only here: if
  your graphs use `x_criterion`, add `python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_criterion.py check --root .` next to the
  gate.

## `kg_audit.py`: the audit package by question (4.22.0)

An auditor asks for the package by question: the answer, the claims, the dated evidence, the gap, and the owner, in a
spreadsheet. The graph already holds all of it; this tool lays it out, one row per questionnaire item, in CSV, XLSX, or
JSON. It does not judge the form (that is `kg_validate.py`) and writes nothing to the graph.

```bash
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_audit.py --root . --questionnaire "Q-2026" --as-of 2026-10-23
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_audit.py --root . --format xlsx --output package.xlsx
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_audit.py --root . --format csv --view evidence > evidence.csv
```

- **The item** is the pair (questionnaire, number) that `x_questionnaire` names (`name` and `questions`). Who comes in:
  - the question: the `question` node with the profile;
  - the answer: a node (not `question`) with the profile for the item, and a node without the profile tied to the
    question by `DEPENDS_ON`, in either direction (both live in real graphs; the answer comes out once). A node with
    the profile has already said which item it answers, so an edge never pulls it into another item;
  - the evidence: a node with `SUPPORTS` to an answer, or with `SUPPORTS` or `TRACES_TO` to the question, to an evidence
    request, or to an evidence requirement of the item, local or from another graph (`external_edges`); a question, a
    request, or a requirement is never evidence;
  - the contradiction: a node with `REFUTES` to the answer or the question. Only a live answer brings evidence and
    contradictions: one that is `superseded` or `refuted` (a refutation already reconciled) neither closes nor opens a
    gap of the item;
  - the evidence request (`role: evidence_request`) and the evidence requirement (`role: evidence_requirement`, "what
    evidence this item requires", in its own column): never taken for a question or an answer. Each piece of evidence
    says which request it came from (the request it points to by `SUPPORTS` or `TRACES_TO`). An item that only a
    request or a requirement cites comes out too, with the gaps of what is missing.
- **The gaps** are computed, never written by hand:
  - `no-answer`: no live answer (an answer that is `refuted` or `superseded` is listed, with its status, but does not
    count);
  - `contradicted`: a `REFUTES` from a node that is neither `refuted` nor `superseded`;
  - `no-confirmed-evidence`: no evidence with `status: confirmed` (evidence that is not confirmed is listed, but does
    not close a gap);
  - `evidence-unstamped`: confirmed evidence without a valid `verified_at`;
  - `evidence-cadence-invalid`: confirmed evidence whose `reverify_every` is not a duration, so it would never be due;
  - `evidence-due`: confirmed evidence whose `verified_at` plus `reverify_every` falls on or before `--as-of` (today by
    default);
  - `verdict-open`: no live verdict, or one other than `meets` and `not_applicable`.
- **Nothing drops in silence.** A node whose `x_questionnaire` lacks `name` or a `questions` list that is not empty, a node whose `role`
  is outside the enum, and a number in `questions` that is not text (`questions: [7]` without quotes) do not come in:
  they come out in `skipped`, in the package itself (the Skipped sheet of the XLSX, `--view skipped` in CSV, the JSON),
  on standard error, and in the human listing, and `--fail-on-gap` gives rc 1 with them.
- **Your own columns.** `--column <key>` adds a key of the answer node (an `x_` key of yours, such as a list of
  remediation cards) as one more column. A list becomes items separated by `; `.
- **The formats.**
  - `csv`: the questions (one row per item) or, with `--view evidence`, the evidence (one row per item and piece of
    evidence, with the problems of its stamp), or, with `--view skipped`, what was skipped, in UTF-8 with a byte-order mark so that Excel reads it. A cell that starts
    with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, a tab, or a carriage return gets a leading apostrophe, so it never runs as a formula (the
    OWASP rule for CSV injection).
  - `xlsx`: the three sheets (questions, evidence, skipped) in one workbook, written with the standard library only, every value as text, the header
    frozen, and a cell cut at Excel's limit of 32,767 UTF-16 units. The same package gives the same bytes.
  - `json`: `kg-ssot.audit/1` (`spec/audit.schema.json`), with everything nested.
  - `human`: a short listing for the terminal.
- **Output and rc.** rc 0 when it exported, 1 when a graph does not read (the package would be incomplete in silence)
  or, with `--fail-on-gap`, when an item has a gap or something was skipped, and 2 on broken input. `xlsx` needs `--output`. Give the corpus with
  `--root`: an edge to another graph resolves by its path from the root.

## `kg_prov_export.py`: provenance in PROV-O

Exports a `.kg.yaml` to [PROV-O](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/) in JSON-LD, for anyone who already uses tools from the
W3C PROV ecosystem. Each node becomes a `prov:Entity`. A node with `provenance` gets `prov:wasDerivedFrom` pointing to
the source and a `prov:Derivation` whose activity carries the `method`; `locator` and `locality` go in as `kg:`
properties. A source that is entirely one http(s) URL becomes the IRI itself; any other source (a path, a command, two
URLs together) becomes a labeled blank node, one per distinct text, so nodes with the same source point to the same
entity.

```bash
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_prov_export.py \
  vendor/kg-ssot/spec/conformance/fixtures/latest/form/method-vocabulary/valid-method-leitura.kg.yaml
```

An excerpt of the output, the node with `provenance`:

```text
   "@id": "urn:kg-ssot:graph:valid-method-leitura#EV_A",
   "@type": "prov:Entity",
   ...
   "prov:wasDerivedFrom": {
    "@id": "_:source0"
   },
   "prov:qualifiedDerivation": {
    "@type": "prov:Derivation",
    "prov:entity": {
     "@id": "_:source0",
     "rdfs:label": "Fonte A"
    },
    "prov:hadActivity": {
     "@type": "prov:Activity",
     "rdfs:label": "leitura: seção 3 do documento A"
    },
    "kg:locator": "caso de conformidade"
   }
```

What it does **not** export, on purpose:

- **The edges.** `SUPPORTS`, `REFUTES`, and the others are evidence relations, and derivation in PROV is a production
  relation. Exporting them as `wasDerivedFrom` would say something the graph does not say.
- **The stamp as a generation time.** `verified_at` comes out as `kg:verifiedAt` (typed `xsd:date` when it is a
  date), not as `prov:generatedAtTime`: in PROV, the generation time marks when the entity came into existence, not
  when it was verified.

The exporter does not validate the graph: run `kg_validate.py` first. `--base IRI` changes the prefix of the node IRIs
(the default is `urn:kg-ssot:graph:`, and each node sits at `<base><meta.id>#<id>`); the `kg:` vocabulary lives at
`urn:kg-ssot:vocab#`, outside that space. rc 2 when the file is unreadable, is not a single YAML document, or has a
malformed `meta` or `nodes`.

## `kg_migrate.py`: the profile-driven migrator

Proposes the `provenance` that contract v4 requires on `confirmed` or PROD nodes that do not have it yet, from a
**profile** that the adopter writes and versions: an ordered list of rules (`spec/kg-migrate-profile.schema.json`),
where the first rule that matches decides. There is a commented example in
`spec/migrate-examples/company-brain.profile.yaml`, measured on a real corpus of 25 graphs and 1,024 nodes.

```bash
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_migrate.py plan  --profile kg-migrate.profile.yaml --out proposals.tsv
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_migrate.py apply --profile kg-migrate.profile.yaml
```

- **`plan` writes nothing.** It prints the counts per rule and, with `--out`, writes the proposal sheet, one row per
  node, with what goes to the reviewer and why. Read the sheet before you run `apply`.
- **Each rule does one of three things:** propose the `provenance`, demote the node to `unverifiable` (the source is
  unrecoverable, which is the contract's default), or only send the node to review. A node that no rule matches also
  goes to review and gets nothing.
- **`when` matches on what the node already carries:** the trace (empty, URL, path, glob, existence in the tree,
  regular expression), the type, the status, the plane, `verified_against`, `source_kind`, and the `SUPPORTS` edges
  that reach the node, with `not` and `any_of`.
- **Templates use the node's fields:** `{trace}`, `{trace_path}`, `{trace_line}`, `{verified_against}`, `{supports}`,
  and `{source_kind}`, and `{a|b}` takes the first one that is not empty. The profile's `note` goes at the end of
  every `method` detail, for example `não reverificado na migração de 2026-10-20` (the note in the example profile).
- **`scopes` gives `verified_scope` only by a list of ids**, never by a text pattern.
- **The profile chooses within the contract and never relaxes it.** Every proposal is checked against the MUST schema
  and the SHOULD form schema before it becomes a proposal. A proposal that would fail goes to review with the reason,
  and so does a template that resolves to empty. A coherence warning that the proposal raises does not block it,
  because the warning tells the truth about the node. For example, a `testemunho` (testimony) on a PROD node raises
  `integrity.testimony-in-prod`: the proposal goes ahead, and the node goes to the reviewer with the warning named.
- **`apply` writes file by file, as text, and comments stay.** Afterward it rereads the file and checks the
  invariance: each node stays as it was, except the keys the action authorizes, and the diff only adds lines, except
  the line of a demoted status. A file that would gain a new MUST code, or a SHOULD warning that the plan did not
  announce, stays as it was. The file's line ending is kept (CRLF stays CRLF), and a file with mixed line endings is
  refused. Running it again changes nothing.
- **Without a list of graphs, the tool reads the `.kg.yaml` files from `git ls-files`.** It leaves out the
  `kg_gate.py` patterns (`*/fixtures/*` and `docs/materials/*`), `vendor/*`, any folder with the `.kg-ssot-version`
  stamp (since 4.20.0), and the `--exclude` globs, with the
  gate's semantics: `fnmatch` on the relative path, where `*` crosses `/`; the profile dialect's `**/`, which matches
  zero folders, also works. `--no-default-excludes` removes the patterns. Note: in the profile's `trace_path_glob`,
  `*` does not cross `/`. A listed graph that does not parse becomes a review row and does not abort the run.
- **A node whose `verified_scope` already matches the profile comes out as `same`**, separate from the nodes that change, and
  `apply` does not touch it.
- **The trace path is lexical and stays inside the repository root.** It is normalized (`./`, `a/../b`), and a path
  that leaves the root with `../` stops being a path. An absolute path or one with `~` counts as nonexistent, without
  looking at the machine's disk.

What stays out, on purpose, because it is judgment: rewriting a label, changing a plane, re-measuring, refuting,
reconciling with `SUPERSEDES`, and promoting an `unverifiable` node. rc 0 when the plan comes out or `apply`
finishes; rc 1 when `apply` refused a file, which stays as it was, with the reason in the report; rc 2 on broken input
(a profile outside the schema, a repeated rule or id, an invalid regular expression, a `when` that would match every
node, a graph given on the command line that does not parse). The migrator travels in the vendor, not in the PyPI or
npm package.

### `keys`: a foreign key becomes `x_<key>` (4.19.0)

```bash
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_migrate.py keys            # the plan: what would be renamed, and what goes to review
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_migrate.py keys --apply    # writes the renames
```

A key the contract does not know fails in the MUST. `keys` renames it to `x_<key>`, the extension prefix, in the top
level, `meta`, nodes, edges, and external edges, by text, so comments stay. The known keys come from the MUST schema of
the release, never from a list in the code. A key goes to the reviewer instead when it is not a slug, when `x_<key>`
already exists in the same mapping, or when the new name is a canonical profile (`severity` would become `x_severity`,
whose value the profile judges). With `--apply`, each file is written only if the reread document equals the old one
with only the renamed keys, the diff touches only those lines, and the file gains no MUST code or SHOULD warning. The
line ending is kept, a file with mixed line endings is refused, and running it again changes nothing. Measured on a copy
of the 15 graphs of the core that failed the MUST on a foreign key: with `meta.title` known since v4.11 and 76 keys
renamed in 12 files, 14 of them pass; the one left also lacks provenance. Run by the core on its own corpus
(2026-10-23), with the gate's excludes: the gate went from 170 to 182 of 184 graphs in the MUST, and the inherited debt
from 14 graphs to 2, both lacking provenance.

### `nest`: your own `x_` keys become a canonical profile (4.21.0)

```bash
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_migrate.py nest --map nest-map.yaml            # the plan
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_migrate.py nest --map nest-map.yaml --apply    # writes the profiles
```

`keys` gives a foreign key the `x_` prefix; `nest` goes one step further and moves the `x_` keys an adopter invented
into the canonical node profiles of [chapter 3](03-format.md), `x_mirror`, `x_doc_cycle`, and `x_questionnaire`. The map
(`spec/kg-migrate-nest.schema.json`) has one rule per profile. A rule applies to the node that has its `when` key, and
each field of the profile comes from one source: `const` (a fixed value), `move` (an `x_` key that leaves the node), or
`copy` (any key, which stays, such as `verified_at`). A source can go through `match` (a regex with one group, read as
ECMA-262 reads it: `\w` and `\d` in ASCII, `\s` with the Unicode spaces, `.` without line breaks, `$` only at the end of
the text; what the two engines read differently is broken input, and a value with a character beyond U+FFFF goes to the
reviewer) and through a value table, `values` for exact values and `prefixes` for the longest matching prefix. With
`raw: true`, the original value of each moved key that had text beyond the code (it came in by a prefix, or the regex
cut part of it) stays in `<profile>.x_raw`; an exact value of the table does not. A key moved through `match` or
`prefixes` loses the text the code leaves out, so such a rule needs `raw: true` (the map is broken input without it):

```yaml
nest_version: "1"
nest:
  - into: x_mirror
    when: x_board_status
    fields:
      system: {const: board}
      state: {move: x_board_status}
      ref: {copy: verified_against, match: "/t/([a-z0-9]+)$"}
      url: {copy: verified_against}
      synced_at: {copy: verified_at}
  - into: x_doc_cycle
    when: x_issuer
    raw: true
    fields:
      issuer: {move: x_issuer}
      state: {move: x_in_force, values: {in force: in_force}, prefixes: {"in force (": in_force}}
```

Nothing is guessed. A node goes to the reviewer, untouched, when a value has no code in the table, when the source of a
required field is missing, when the node already has the profile, when the profile it would get fails the profile's
SHOULD schema (a `synced_at` that is not a date, a `state` outside the enum), when the node is written in flow style
(`{...}`), when its `when` key is null, when a value is `.nan` or `.inf`, or when the text edit of that node would not
reread the same (a moved value with an anchor `&x` or an alias `*x`). The plan tries the text edit of the whole file
once, and splits it only when it fails, so a node it cannot edit goes to the reviewer there, and `--apply` writes the
others. `--apply` writes each file under the same checks as `keys`: the reread document must equal the old one with only
the moved keys and the new profiles, and the file must gain no MUST code or SHOULD warning. The line ending is kept,
comments outside the moved keys stay, and running it again changes nothing. Measured on a copy of an adopter's two
graphs (108 nodes with 168 such keys): 106 profiles built, 2 left for the reviewer (two `x_in_force` values with free
text the map did not cover), both files written with the same verdict as before.


========== docs/manual/06-adoption-and-ci.md ==========

# 6. Adoption and CI

**English** | [Português (Brasil)](pt-BR/06-adocao-e-ci.md)

[← Tools](05-tools.md) · [Index](README.md) · [Conformance and readers →](07-conformance-and-readers.md)

This chapter is the map. The full guide, with every edge case, is [`ADOPTING.md`](../../ADOPTING.md).

## The four-step path

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["1. vendor update<br/>brings in the tag"] --> B["2. git add vendor/<br/>+ gate --update"]
  B --> C["3. commit<br/>vendor + baseline"]
  C --> D["4. CI: check + gate<br/>on every PR"]
```

Run this at the root of your repository, with Python 3.11 or later (`rpds-py`, a jsonschema dependency, declares
`Requires-Python >=3.11`):

```bash
# 1. bring in the release, by tag, from the public repository
git clone https://github.com/marciocar/kg-ssot ../kg-ssot
python3 -I -B ../kg-ssot/tools/kg_vendor.py update --tag kg-ssot-v4.22.0 --dest vendor/kg-ssot

# 2. the dependencies in a venv, then the baseline (the gate only measures tracked files: git add first)
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install --require-hashes -r vendor/kg-ssot/tools/requirements.txt
echo .venv/ >> .gitignore
git add vendor/kg-ssot .gitignore docs/          # and your .kg.yaml files, wherever they live
.venv/bin/python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_gate.py --update

# 3. commit the vendor, with its stamp, and the baseline
git add .kg-ssot/gate && git commit -m "adopt the KG-SSOT contract"
```

Graphs that already fail become inherited debt, named by path. Step 4 is CI, on every PR. The full GitHub Actions
workflow is in section 3 of [`ADOPTING.md`](../../ADOPTING.md#3-the-ci-step), the CI step. The step itself is:

```yaml
- name: KG-SSOT contract (intact vendor + per-graph gate)
  run: |
    pip install --require-hashes -r vendor/kg-ssot/tools/requirements.txt
    python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_vendor.py check --dest vendor/kg-ssot
    python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_gate.py
```

## What the gate guarantees

- No **new** graph gets in while it fails MUST.
- No inherited graph gains a MUST code it did not have.
- The SHOULD debt, by code, does not go up.
- A contract change shows up in the PR: the baseline records the name and the sha256 of the schemas.

Fixing one graph does not make up for breaking another: the gate compares MUST graph by graph.

The gate measures only `.kg.yaml` files. A `.kg.json` file in the repository stays outside it. If you want CI to
check those files, run `kg_validate.py` on them in a step of its own.

## Output language in CI

Since 4.18.0, the tools print human output in English by default. They print it in Brazilian Portuguese when
`KG_SSOT_LANG=pt-BR` is set or the locale is `pt_BR`. The tools read the language in gettext order: `KG_SSOT_LANG`,
`LANGUAGE`, `LC_ALL`, `LC_MESSAGES`, `LANG`. The first variable that is set decides; an empty one is skipped. `C`,
`POSIX`, and a language with no catalog mean English.

Base the decision on the return code, never on the text. The gate returns rc 0 when nothing got worse, rc 1 when
something got worse, and rc 2 on broken input. Here is a failing gate in English, after a new graph that
fails MUST entered the PR (rc 1):

```text
✗ WORSE  docs/new.kg.yaml fails MUST: form.required.node.label
· 3 graphs; 1 pass MUST; 1 in the inherited debt
  MUST   docs/legacy.kg.yaml (inherited): form.required.node.plane
  MUST   docs/new.kg.yaml (new): form.required.node.label
```

With `KG_SSOT_LANG=pt-BR`, the same run prints `✗ PIOROU` in place of `✗ WORSE`. If a CI step searches the output
for text (`✗ WORSE` or `GATE BROKEN` from the gate, `PASS` or `BROKEN INPUT` from `kg_validate.py`), set
`KG_SSOT_LANG` in that step or match both languages. Data does not change language: the JSON keys, the codes, and
the place in a verdict (`nó X`, `aresta #n`) stay the same; only the `message` and `hint` text follows the language.

## Update the tag

Do it all in one PR:

1. Run `kg_vendor.py update` with the new tag. From inside the vendor, pass
   `--source https://github.com/marciocar/kg-ssot`.
2. Run `git add vendor/kg-ssot`.
3. Run `kg_vendor.py check --dest vendor/kg-ssot --index` to verify what the commit will carry. If you come from a
   tag older than 4.8.1, run `update` twice: the old kit does not write the vendor's `.gitattributes`, and the 4.8.1
   kit does.
4. Run `kg_gate.py` to see the difference.
5. Run `kg_gate.py --update` to record the new identity.

If a minor version brings a SHOULD warning that your corpus already had, the debt goes up by design. In that case,
run `--update` with `--accept-regression "<reason>"`.

## Move up a major version (v3 → v4)

v4 fails what v3 only warned about. You move up by the **ramp**: the graphs that start to fail enter the baseline
as inherited debt, and from then on the debt only shrinks. There is no date trick in the schema, and you do not
fix the whole corpus at once. The step-by-step guide, with the commands, is in section 5 of
[`ADOPTING.md`](../../ADOPTING.md#5-from-v3-to-v4), from v3 to v4.

## Environment note

On systems with PEP 668 (Ubuntu 24.04 and later), `pip install` outside a venv is refused. Use a venv and run the
kit with its Python. On GitHub Actions with `actions/setup-python`, `pip install` works directly.

## In an app

KG-SSOT holds **knowledge about the product**: decisions, business rules, claims, and the evidence for each one.
It is not a runtime database. A user's progress, points, and streak stay in the app's database. What goes into the
graph is, for example, "the streak resets after a day with no entry," with the source of the decision, the date it
was verified, and a `TRACES_TO` edge to the code or test that implements it. The recipe is in
[chapter 8](08-recipes.md#a-business-rule-linked-to-code), "A business rule linked to code."

- **In CI:** the path above works for any repository, in any language. The gate only needs Python in CI.
- **At runtime, in Python, through the package:** since 4.9.0, the kit also ships on PyPI as `kg-ssot`
  (`pip install kg-ssot`). The modules live in `kg_ssot`, and the package installs the commands `kg-validate`,
  `kg-conformance`, `kg-gate`, `kg-store`, `kg-query`, `kg-diff`, `kg-mcp`, and `kg-prov-export`. The contract and
  the suite travel inside the package:

  ```python
  from kg_ssot import kg_store
  store = kg_store.GitStore("/var/lib/my-app/graphs", init=True)   # outside the app's repository
  ```

  The package is the path for the app. For the **gate in CI**, vendoring by tag is still the recommended channel,
  because the contract that judges the graph stays in the repository's diff.
- **At runtime, in Python, through the vendor:** put `vendor/kg-ssot/tools` on `sys.path` and run without writing
  bytecode, so the vendor `check` stays intact:

  ```python
  import sys
  sys.dont_write_bytecode = True                    # or PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 in the environment
  sys.path.insert(0, "vendor/kg-ssot/tools")
  import kg_store                                    # the store that only writes what the contract approves
  store = kg_store.GitStore("/var/lib/my-app/graphs", init=True)   # outside the app's repository
  ```

  Keep the store root **outside** the app's repository. Inside a git repository, `DiskStore` and `VersionedStore`
  refuse the root. `GitStore` with its root at the repository itself commits on whatever branch is checked out,
  outside the PR, and in a subfolder of the repository it creates a nested git repository.
- **In JavaScript (Node, React Native, Expo):** since 4.9.0, the JS reader ships on npm as `kg-ssot`
  (`npm install kg-ssot`). Its entry point imports nothing from Node, and the contract validator comes precompiled,
  with no `new Function` and no `eval`, so it runs on Hermes. `verdict(text, { format })` returns the MUST verdict
  with the suite's codes, and the `kg-ssot-validate` command judges files. Since 4.10.0, it also measures SHOULD
  warnings, with the same codes as the reference reader in every suite case. Line numbers and hints stay with the
  Python reference reader.
- **In an MCP client, such as Claude Desktop:** since 4.9.0, the reference MCP server also ships as an MCP Bundle
  (`kg-ssot-<version>.mcpb`). It is attached to the tag's release in the public repository after the `kg-ssot`
  package of the same version is on PyPI, because the bundle installs the package from there. During install, the
  client asks for the store directory and whether the server is read-only, and it installs the package with `uv` on
  your machine. `uv` creates the environment inside the extension folder, locked by a `uv.lock` with the hash of
  every dependency. The bundle carries GitHub's provenance attestation
  (`gh attestation verify kg-ssot-<version>.mcpb --repo marciocar/kg-ssot`) and is listed in the official MCP
  Registry as `io.github.marciocar/kg-ssot`. The store is the versioned one: every write is recorded, and
  `kg_history` shows it. A folder inside a git repository uses git, in a nested repository (the outer repository
  then sees it as an untracked folder). When the folder does not open, the server starts with judging only and
  tells the model why, and the model reports it in the chat (since 4.9.1; in 4.9.0 the reason went only to the log).
  It runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows. On Windows, the store runs since 4.9.1 (in 4.9.0 it did not open there),
  with the path protection described in [chapter 5](05-tools.md). The server runs locally, over stdio, and talks
  to no external service.
- **In another language:** there is no ready-made reader beyond Python and JavaScript. Validate through the CLI
  (`kg_validate.py --format json` returns the JSON verdict of `spec/verdict.schema.json`) or through a model, with
  the MCP server (`kg_mcp.py`). Your own reader proves it agrees with the contract by passing the suite
  ([chapter 7](07-conformance-and-readers.md)).


========== docs/manual/07-conformance-and-readers.md ==========

# 7. Conformance and readers

**English** | [Português (Brasil)](pt-BR/07-conformidade-e-leitores.md)

[← Adoption and CI](06-adoption-and-ci.md) · [Index](README.md) · [Recipes →](08-recipes.md)

The contract applies to **every reader** of `.kg.yaml`: a viewer, an extractor, a JavaScript port, a Go validator.
A reader proves it follows the contract by passing the suite, not by reading the specification and feeling sure it
understood. The full reference is [`spec/conformance/README.md`](../../spec/conformance/README.md).

## How the suite is built

- Each **group** is a folder with a `manifest.json` and one real `.kg.yaml` (or `.kg.json`) per case. The file is
  real so that any CLI reads it the way it would read an actual graph.
- Each case declares `valid`, the expected `codes` (MUST), and the expected `warnings` (SHOULD). `warnings` is
  optional, and a missing list counts as `[]`.
- **One case, one defect.** A reader passes a case when the **set** of codes it emits **equals** the expected set.
  Equality, not inclusion: a reader that flags everything does not pass. Order and repetition do not count.
- The suite validates itself: `manifest.schema.json` checks every manifest, and `metaschema-tests/` holds manifests
  the schema must accept and others it must reject.

```json
{
  "description": "Os enums do nó.",
  "layer": "form",
  "pending_on": [],
  "cases": [
    {
      "file": "bad-node-type-enum.kg.yaml",
      "description": "node_type fora do enum",
      "valid": false,
      "codes": [
        "form.enum.node.node_type"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

| Folder | What it means |
|---|---|
| `fixtures/latest/` | The current contract. Every reader **must** pass |
| `fixtures/optional/` | Behavior a reader **may** implement. It reports and does not fail |
| `fixtures/proposals/` | Cases that depend on an open decision. It is empty today |

## Write a reader

1. **Parse.** Read YAML with YAML 1.2 booleans, a single document, and a mapping at the root. A duplicate key
   fails (`1` and `"1"` collide). `.nan` and `.inf` fail. A `.kg.json` file goes through a JSON parser under the
   contract's JSON profile.
2. **Form.** Convert to canonical JSON (dates as ISO text, keys as text) and validate against
   `kg-contract-v4.schema.json`, with `format` as an **assertion**. Warnings come from
   `kg-contract-v4.should.schema.json`.
3. **Integrity.** Check unique ids, existing endpoints (`from`, `to`, `trigger`), no node of degree 0, the endpoints
   of `external_edges`, and the `integrity.*` warnings that span fields or edges.
4. **Codes.** Map each error to its stable code. The code table and the naming rules are in
   [chapter 4](04-contract.md#codes) and in the suite reference.

The reference reader, [`tools/kg_validate.py`](../../tools/kg_validate.py), is the model. Its comments explain
each rule, so you can read it alongside the suite.

### Three traps the suite catches

- **Text length in code points.** The 280-character limit on `label` counts code points, like JSON Schema
  `maxLength`. An emoji counts as 1. JavaScript `str.length` counts it as 2.
- **`format: date` as an annotation.** Many validators skip format checks by default. Here a bad date fails.
- **`$` before a line break.** The `pattern` values follow ECMA-262 semantics: `$` does not match before a trailing
  line break, unlike Python's `re`.

## Run the suite with your reader

`kg_conformance.py` runs only the reference reader, and the kit ships no tool that runs an outside reader over the
suite. Your reader runs the suite with its own code: it iterates over the `manifest.json` files in `fixtures/latest/`, judges each case
(with the repository root at `<manifest folder>/<corpus>` when the case declares `corpus`), and compares the sets of
`codes` and `warnings` for equality. A reader that does not expose codes compares only the verdict: `valid: true`
means accept, and `valid: false` means reject.

## The runner contract

So that the maintainer can measure your reader next to the reference reader, case by case, your reader exposes a
**runner**: `runner <case>` prints one JSON object on the last line of stdout and exits with rc 0.

```json
{"verdict": "accept", "codes": [], "warnings": [], "detail": ""}
```

- `verdict`: `accept`, `reject`, or `error`. This is level 1, and every reader has it.
- `codes` and `warnings`: the lists of codes, or `null` if the reader does not say why. This is level 2.
- A case that declares `corpus` in its manifest arrives as `runner <case> --corpus <dir>`.
- Output that is not JSON, an unknown `verdict`, an rc other than 0, or a timeout counts as `error`.

A reader that only gives the verdict is already comparable at level 1. Exposing the codes is level 2, and it is what
lets you diagnose a divergence.


========== docs/manual/08-recipes.md ==========

# 8. Recipes

**English** | [Português (Brasil)](pt-BR/08-receitas.md)

[← Conformance and readers](07-conformance-and-readers.md) · [Index](README.md) · [Troubleshooting →](09-troubleshooting.md)

## Write your first graph

A question and the evidence that supports it. The evidence is `confirmed`, so it carries `provenance`.

```yaml
meta:
  schema_version: "1"
  id: example
  baseline: "2026-10-12"
  review_after: "2027-01-12"
nodes:
  - id: Q_CACHE_TTL
    node_type: question
    plane: DEV
    status: open
    impact: 3
    confidence: 0.5
    label: Does the session cache need a TTL?
  - id: E_CACHE_GROWTH
    node_type: evidence
    plane: DEV
    status: confirmed
    impact: 3
    confidence: 0.9
    label: Without a TTL, cache memory grows 40 MB per hour in the load test.
    trace: bench/cache-load.md
    verified_at: "2026-10-12"
    provenance:
      source: bench/cache-load.md
      locator: table 2
      method: "medição: 4-hour load test"
edges:
  - from: E_CACHE_GROWTH
    to: Q_CACHE_TTL
    edge_type: SUPPORTS
```

The `method` starts with its class, `medição` (measurement), followed by the detail.

Every node needs at least one edge: a node on its own fails as `integrity.orphan-node`. That is why a graph with a
single node does not pass, and why your first graph starts with a question and what supports it.

With the venv from [adoption](06-adoption-and-ci.md) active (`. .venv/bin/activate`), or with `.venv/bin/python3`
in place of `python3`:

```bash
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_validate.py docs/example.kg.yaml
```

```text
PASS docs/example.kg.yaml
· 1 files; 1 pass the MUST; 0 with a SHOULD warning (kg-contract-v4.schema.json + kg-contract-v4.should.schema.json)
```

## Fix a node that fails

This production node failed with `form.required.node.provenance` and `form.unknown-key.node.priority`, and it
warned with `form.required.node.verified_against`:

```yaml
  - id: C_RETRY_SAFE
    node_type: claim
    plane: PROD
    status: confirmed
    impact: 4
    confidence: 0.8
    label: The payment retry is idempotent.
    verified_at: "2026-10-01"
    owner: payments-team
    priority: high
```

The fix: your own key gets the `x_` prefix, the stamp gets a target, and the provenance says where the claim came
from.

```yaml
    verified_at: "2026-10-01"
    owner: payments-team
    x_priority: high
    verified_against: tests/payment_retry_test.py
    provenance:
      source: tests/payment_retry_test.py
      locator: test_retry_is_idempotent
      method: "medição: integration test in CI"
```

## Record a report without making up a measurement

Someone on the team said the retry is idempotent, and nobody ran anything. The class is `testemunho` (testimony):

```yaml
    provenance:
      source: payments team
      locator: conversation on 2026-10-01
      method: "testemunho: report from the payments team"
```

On a PROD node, the contract warns (`integrity.testimony-in-prod`): production backed only by a report is a risk the
graph should show, not hide.

```bash
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_validate.py --where testimony.kg.yaml
```

```text
PASS testimony.kg.yaml
  SHOULD integrity.testimony-in-prod ×1
    SHOULD integrity.testimony-in-prod  nó C_RETRY_SAFE
· 1 files; 1 pass the MUST; 1 with a SHOULD warning (kg-contract-v4.schema.json + kg-contract-v4.should.schema.json)
```

## A node with no source at all

Do not write `source: unknown`: that fails. Set the node's `status` to `unverifiable` instead. It stays valid
without `provenance`, even in PROD, and the graph tells the truth: the claim has no recoverable origin.

## Hand a node to an agent without losing its status

A node's label is a claim, and its `status` says where that claim stands. A label like `The supplier does not meet
item 4.2` on an `open` node is a claim under review. If the tool that serves the graph to an agent sends only the
label, the agent reads it as fact. An adopter found this defect while testing a chat: the graph lookup sent the label
of an `open` `claim`, and the model answered that the supplier did not meet the item.

**A claim never travels without its status.** When you summarize a node for another tool (an MCP tool, a prompt, a
report), include at least the `status`. When the answer depends on how strong the evidence is, include the `method`
class too. Then tell the agent, in its instructions, what each status means:

```text
C_ITEM_42 [claim · open] The supplier does not meet item 4.2.
  → under review: do not assert it; say it is being analyzed.
C_ITEM_17 [claim · confirmed · leitura] The supplier meets item 1.7.
  → confirmed by reading the document.
```

The `kg_get` tool in `kg_mcp.py` returns the whole graph, with the `status` of every node. The risk lies in the layer
you write on top of it, when you summarize.

## Link a decision to a question in another graph

```yaml
meta:
  schema_version: "1"
  id: decision
nodes:
  - id: D_CACHE_TTL_15MIN
    node_type: decision
    plane: DEV
    status: open
    impact: 3
    confidence: 0.7
    label: A 15-minute TTL on the session cache.
    trace: docs/adr/0009-cache-ttl.md
edges: []
external_edges:
  - from: D_CACHE_TTL_15MIN
    to: docs/example.kg.yaml#Q_CACHE_TTL
    edge_type: TRACES_TO
```

Validate it with the corpus, so the reader checks the external end. In a git repository, the corpus is the tracked
graphs, so the target graph has to be in git:

```bash
git add docs/example.kg.yaml
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_validate.py --corpus . docs/decision.kg.yaml
```

With an id that does not exist in the other graph, the reader fails the file:

```text
FAIL docs/wrong.kg.yaml
  MUST   integrity.dangling-external ×1
· 1 files; 0 pass the MUST; 0 with a SHOULD warning (kg-contract-v4.schema.json + kg-contract-v4.should.schema.json)
```

## Lock in the gain after paying down debt

Fixed an inherited graph? The gate passes and asks for `--update`. Run it in the same PR:

```bash
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_gate.py --update
```

Without it, a future PR could break that graph again and the gate would not notice, because the graph would still sit
in the inherited debt.

## Find every node with a given code

```bash
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_validate.py --where docs/*.kg.yaml
```

Each indented line carries the code and the node, so you can filter with `grep`.

## A business rule linked to code

In an app, the rule lives in the graph, together with the decision it came from and the code that implements it. Here
is the streak rule of a habit app: the product decision, the domain rule with the test that measures it, and the code
file.

```yaml
meta:
  schema_version: "1"
  id: streak
  baseline: "2026-10-13"
  review_after: "2027-01-13"
nodes:
  - id: D_STREAK_RESET
    node_type: decision
    plane: PROD
    status: done
    impact: 4
    confidence: 0.9
    label: The streak resets after one full day with no entry, in the user's time zone.
    trace: docs/decisions/2026-10-streak.md
    verified_at: "2026-10-13"
    provenance:
      source: docs/decisions/2026-10-streak.md
      locator: Decision section
      method: "leitura: product decision record"
  - id: R_STREAK_RESET
    node_type: rule
    layer: domain
    plane: PROD
    status: confirmed
    impact: 4
    confidence: 0.9
    label: streak.reset() runs when the last entry is older than yesterday in the user's time zone.
    verified_at: "2026-10-13"
    provenance:
      source: tests/test_streak.py
      locator: test_resets_after_a_day_with_no_entry
      method: "medição: pytest tests/test_streak.py, 6 cases passing"
  - id: A_STREAK_CODE
    node_type: artifact
    layer: domain
    plane: PROD
    status: confirmed
    impact: 3
    confidence: 0.9
    label: The streak implementation lives in app/streak.py.
    verified_at: "2026-10-13"
    verified_against: app/streak.py
    provenance:
      source: app/streak.py
      locator: reset function
      method: "leitura: code at the release commit"
edges:
  - from: R_STREAK_RESET
    to: D_STREAK_RESET
    edge_type: TRACES_TO
  - from: R_STREAK_RESET
    to: A_STREAK_CODE
    edge_type: TRACES_TO
```

```bash
python3 -I -B vendor/kg-ssot/tools/kg_validate.py docs/streak.kg.yaml
```

```text
PASS docs/streak.kg.yaml
· 1 files; 1 pass the MUST; 0 with a SHOULD warning (kg-contract-v4.schema.json + kg-contract-v4.should.schema.json)
```

The contract checks the form, the edges, and the provenance. It does not run your test or read your code: the app's CI
runs `tests/test_streak.py`. The graph records what was measured, when, and how (`method`), and `verified_at` tells
you how long ago. When the rule changes, the PR that changes the code changes the node too, and the diff shows both
together.


========== docs/manual/09-troubleshooting.md ==========

# 9. Troubleshooting

**English** | [Português (Brasil)](pt-BR/09-problemas.md)

[← Recipes](08-recipes.md) · [Index](README.md) · [Glossary →](10-glossary.md)

Run `kg_validate.py --where <file>` first. It tells you the code and the node.

## Common MUST codes

| Code | What it means | How to fix it |
|---|---|---|
| `form.required.node.provenance` | A `confirmed` or PROD node has no `provenance` | Add `source`, `locator` and `method`. If there is no source, change the status to `unverifiable` |
| `form.pattern.node.provenance.source` | `source` is a placeholder (`unknown`, `n/a`, `tbd`, `?`...) | Use the real source. If no source can be recovered, remove the `provenance` and use `unverifiable` |
| `form.unknown-key.node.<key>` | The key is not in the grammar | Prefix it with `x_`, or use the contract field (for example, `narrative`) |
| `form.required.node.<field>` | One of the seven required fields is missing | Add the field |
| `form.enum.node.<field>` | The value is not in the list (`node_type`, `plane`, `status`) | See the lists in [chapter 3](03-format.md) |
| `form.pattern.node.verified_at` | The date has the wrong format, or does not exist on the calendar | Use `YYYY-MM-DD`, in quotes |
| `integrity.orphan-node` | A node has no edge at all | Every node needs at least one edge: in `edges`, set `from:` to its id, `to:` to the id of another node, and `edge_type` to the relation (`TRACES_TO`, `SUPPORTS`, `DEPENDS_ON`...). If there is no relation, remove the node. `--where` shows the fix with the id |
| `integrity.dangling-to` · `-from` · `-trigger` · `-on` | The edge (or its trigger) points to an id that does not exist | Fix the id, or create the node |
| `integrity.duplicate-id` | Two nodes have the same id | Rename one of them |
| `integrity.dangling-external-local` | The local end of an `external_edges` entry does not exist in this file | Fix the id |
| `integrity.dangling-external` | The external end does not exist in the corpus | Fix the path or the id after `#`. Or the target graph is not in git yet (`git add`) |
| `yaml.forbidden-key-on` | An edge has the `on` key | Replace it with `trigger` |
| `parse.duplicate-key` | A key repeats in the same mapping | Remove the duplicate |
| `parse.not-single-document` | The file has more than one YAML document (`---`) | Keep one graph per file |
| `parse.yaml-error` | The YAML does not parse (or goes past the nesting or alias limit). In the contract profile, this also covers a tab outside quotes, block scalars and comments, a `!` tag with no name, and a `!!timestamp` that is not a date | Fix the syntax on the line the error points to. Replace the tab with spaces, and put the date in quotes |
| `parse.empty-document` · `parse.root-not-mapping` | The file is empty, or the root is not a mapping | A graph starts with `meta:`, `nodes:` and `edges:` |

The full list, with the shape of each code, is in
[`spec/conformance/README.md`](../../spec/conformance/README.md#codes).

## Common SHOULD warnings

| Code | How to fix it |
|---|---|
| `yaml.unquoted-date` | Put dates in quotes: `"2026-10-12"` |
| `yaml.unsafe-integer` | An integer goes past ±(2^53−1), and a JavaScript reader loses the exact value. Write it as text, in quotes. In `.kg.json`, it fails |
| `yaml.lone-surrogate` | The text has a lone surrogate (U+D800 to U+DFFF without its pair). Fix the text. In `.kg.json`, it fails |
| `yaml.depth-over-128` | The file nests more than 128 collections. Flatten the structure. In `.kg.json`, it fails |
| `form.range.node.label` | Shorten the `label` to 280 characters or less, and move the rest to `narrative` |
| `form.pattern.node.provenance.method` | Use `<class>: <detail>`, with the class in `medição` (measurement), `leitura` (reading), `juízes` (judges), `derivado` (derived) or `testemunho` (testimony). It fails in v5 |
| `form.required.node.verified_against` | Add `verified_against`: say what you checked on the `verified_at` date |
| `form.required.node.verified_at` | A PROD node has no `verified_at`, or has `verified_scope` without the date. Stamp the last check |
| `form.enum.node.verified_scope` | Use `fato`, `mecanismo` or `nenhum` |
| `integrity.untraced-decision` | Give the decision an origin: `trace`, `provenance` or a `TRACES_TO` edge |
| `integrity.refutes-unreconciled` | The node receives `REFUTES` and is still live: the graph asserts and refutes the same thing. If the refutation holds, change the target's status to `refuted` or `superseded`. If it does not, remove the edge or change the status of the refuting node. Today this is a warning, and it will fail in a future contract version |
| `integrity.verified-before-fact` | `verified_at` is earlier than `valid_from`. If the fact takes effect in the future (a regulation read before it comes into force), the warning is expected and can stay in the gate baseline. If not, the dates are swapped: `valid_from` is when the fact started to hold, and `verified_at` is when you checked it |
| `integrity.testimony-in-prod` | Measure it and change the class to `medição`, or accept the risk in plain sight |

## The gate

| Symptom | Cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `GATE BROKEN  missing baseline (.kg-ssot/gate): write the first one with --update` (pt-BR: `GATE QUEBRADO  linha de base ausente`) | There is no `.kg-ssot/gate/` (and no `.kg-ssot/gate.json` from before 4.16.0) | Run `kg_gate.py --update` and commit the baseline |
| `· identity contract_sha256: the baseline is from …` (pt-BR: `· identidade contract_sha256: a base é de …`) | The new tag changed the schemas, but no verdict changed | Nothing to do. Write the new identity with `kg_gate.py --update` whenever you want |
| Merge conflict in `.kg-ssot/gate.json` | The baseline from before 4.16.0 is a single file | Upgrade to 4.16.0 or later and run `kg_gate.py --update`: the baseline becomes the folder, with one record per graph |
| Conflict in `.kg-ssot/gate/contract.json`, or modify/delete on `gate.json`, in the first merge after the migration | One branch migrated to the folder while the other still changed `gate.json` | Keep the folder, run `git rm .kg-ssot/gate.json` and `kg_gate.py --update`. Migrate the live branches before you merge to avoid the conflict |
| A new graph does not show up in the measurement | The gate only measures tracked files | Run `git add` on the graph |
| `✗ WORSE` (pt-BR: `✗ PIOROU`) on a graph you did not touch | The contract moved to a new tag, and the graph now fails | Write the new baseline with `--update`. A regression needs `--accept-regression "<reason>"` |
| The vendor's fixtures ended up in the corpus | You used `--no-default-excludes` | Drop the option, or pass `--exclude` |

## The vendor

| Symptom | Cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `check` returns rc 1 even though you edited nothing | A tool that imported the kit wrote a `.pyc` into the vendor | Delete the `__pycache__` and run everything with `python3 -I -B` |
| `update` refuses to replace the vendor | The target has no stamp, or the vendor diverges from it | With no stamp, the target is not a vendor, and `--force` does not help: pick another `--dest`, or move the directory out of the way yourself. If it diverges, run `check` to see what changed. Use `--force` only if the local edit can go away |
| `update` fails when run from inside the vendor | `--source` is missing | Pass `--source https://github.com/marciocar/kg-ssot` |

## Environment

`pip install` fails with `externally-managed-environment`: create a venv (`python3 -m venv .venv`) and use its
Python. See the details in [chapter 6](06-adoption-and-ci.md#environment-note).


========== docs/manual/10-glossary.md ==========

# 10. Glossary

**English** | [Português (Brasil)](pt-BR/10-glossario.md)

[← Troubleshooting](09-troubleshooting.md) · [Index](README.md)

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Adopter** | A repository that brings in the contract by tag and runs the gate in CI |
| **Audit package** | One row per questionnaire item, with the question, the answer, the verdict, the dated evidence, the evidence requests, the owner, and the computed gaps, in CSV, XLSX, or JSON (`kg_audit.py`), since 4.22.0 |
| **Baseline** | The `.kg-ssot/gate/` folder with the debt the gate compares against: the contract identity and one record per graph (through 4.15.1, the single file `.kg-ssot/gate.json`) |
| **Canonical profile** | The shape the SHOULD gives to an `x_` key that adopters repeat (`x_term`, `x_mirror`, `x_severity`...), since v4.11; `x_criterion` and `x_measured_under` since v4.12. It only judges a key that is present, and only warns |
| **Class (of `method`)** | `medição` (measurement), `leitura` (reading), `juízes` (judges), `derivado` (derived), or `testemunho` (testimony) |
| **Code** | The stable identifier of a violation, such as `form.required.node.label` |
| **Conformance suite** | The cases in `spec/conformance/` that every reader must pass |
| **Contract** | The MUST and SHOULD schemas, plus the YAML profile rules and the integrity rules |
| **Corpus** | The set of graphs (`.kg.yaml` and `.kg.json`) in a repository |
| **External edge** | An edge in `external_edges`, with one end in another graph of the same repository |
| **`gate` profile** | The minimal part of the release: just enough to run the gate and the check |
| **Graph** | A `.kg.yaml` file, or its JSON form, a `.kg.json` file |
| **Inherited debt** | The graphs that already failed MUST when the baseline was recorded |
| **MUST** | The contract level that fails |
| **Node** | A typed claim in the graph |
| **Orphan** | A node with no edges. It fails |
| **Plane** | `DEV` or `PROD` |
| **Pre-registered criterion** | A yardstick fixed before the data, one node per version (`x_criterion`, with its `sha256`); a result cites the version it was measured under (`x_measured_under`), and a change after seeing the data is a dated amendment, since v4.12 |
| **Provenance** | The `provenance` object (`source`, `locator`, `method`): where the claim came from |
| **Ramp** | Two senses: (1) in the contract, a warning in one version about what will fail in the next; (2) in adoption, moving up a major version by recording what started to fail as debt, and paying it down over time |
| **Ratchet** | A check that only lets the measure improve or stay the same. The gate is the per-graph ratchet |
| **Reader** | Any program that reads `.kg.yaml` (or `.kg.json`). The reference reader is `kg_validate.py` |
| **Release** | A `kg-ssot-vX.Y.Z` tag with the surface listed in `spec/release.json` |
| **Runner** | The command that exposes a reader to the suite: `runner <case>` prints a JSON object with the verdict |
| **SHOULD** | The contract level that only warns |
| **SHOULD debt** | How many graphs (or occurrences) carry each warning |
| **Synonym** | An item of `x_term.labels`: another way to write the term, `alt` or `hidden`, with its own source, document version, and verification date |
| **Term** | A node with the `x_term` profile: the preferred label of a concept in a domain vocabulary, with its synonyms |
| **Testimony** | The `testemunho` class: an account from someone, or a third-party measurement that you only read |
| **Vendor** | The copy of the release inside the adopter, in `vendor/kg-ssot`, verified by `check` |
| **Vendor stamp** | The `.kg-ssot-version` file with the tag, the commit, the version, the contract, and the sha256 of each vendored file |
| **Verification stamp** | The pair `verified_at` and `verified_against` on a node |
| **`x_`** | The extension prefix: keys that start with it pass freely |


========== spec/conformance/README.md ==========

# Conformance suite for `.kg.yaml` and `.kg.json`

**English** | [Português (Brasil)](README.pt-BR.md)

> The cases measure contract v4: `spec/kg-contract-v4.schema.json` (MUST) and
> `spec/kg-contract-v4.should.schema.json` (SHOULD).

Every `.kg.yaml` reader must pass this suite: the reference reader `tools/kg_validate.py`, a viewer, a graph
extractor, or a port to another language. The cases are **pure data**, modeled on the
[JSON-Schema-Test-Suite](https://github.com/json-schema-org/JSON-Schema-Test-Suite), and they do not depend on any
agent harness.

## Format

A **group** is a folder with a `manifest.json` and one real `.kg.yaml` (or `.kg.json`) file per case. Each case is a
real file, not text embedded in the JSON, so any CLI can take the path and read it the way it reads a real graph.

```json
{
  "description": "enums do nó",
  "layer": "form",
  "pending_on": [],
  "cases": [
    { "file": "bad-node-type-enum.kg.yaml",
      "description": "node_type fora do enum",
      "valid": false,
      "codes": ["form.enum.node.node_type"],
      "warnings": [] }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `description` | Group and case. Required, non-empty text. It can carry the contract-version mark described below. |
| `layer` | Group. `parse`, `form`, `integrity`, `yaml`, or `semantic`: the layer the group exercises. `semantic` exists only in `optional/`. |
| `pending_on` | Group. Ids of the open decisions the verdict depends on. Empty in `latest/`, non-empty in `proposals/`. |
| `cases` | Group. The list of cases, with at least one. |
| `file` | Case. The case file, next to the manifest: a lowercase slug ending in `.kg.yaml`, `.yaml`, or `.kg.json`. |
| `corpus` | Case, optional (v4.3). A directory, relative to the manifest, that acts as the repository root when the reader checks the external end of `external_edges`. |
| `valid` | Case. `true` requires `codes: []`. `false` requires at least one code. |
| `codes` | Case. **MUST** violations: they fail the file. |
| `warnings` | Case. **SHOULD** violations: they only warn, and the file stays valid. Optional; when absent, it counts as `[]`. |

`manifest.schema.json` (JSON Schema 2020-12) validates every manifest. The suite validates itself with the same
technology as the contract, the way the JSON-Schema-Test-Suite does in its own CI. `metaschema-tests/` holds the
manifests the metaschema must accept (`good/`) and the ones it must reject (`bad/`).

**One case, one defect.** A reader passes a case when the **set** of codes it emits **equals** the expected set, in
both `codes` and `warnings`. Equality, not inclusion: a reader that flags everything cannot pass. Order and repetition
do not count.

**The description marks the contract version a case requires**, at the group or case level, in one of these forms:
"Desde o v4.6", "(v4.6)", or "do v4.6". The maintainer's check requires the highest mark to equal the version the
reference reader declares (`CONTRACT_VERSION` in `tools/kg_validate.py`), and requires the description of one of the
schemas to declare it ("No v4.6"). This way, a new rule that only the reader sees still changes the bytes of the
schemas, which `kg_gate.py` keeps as the contract identity.

## Codes

Each code is a stable slug per layer, and the metaschema checks its shape.

| Layer | Shape | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| parse | `parse.<reason>` | `parse.yaml-error`, `parse.duplicate-key`, `parse.empty-document`, `parse.not-single-document`, `parse.root-not-mapping` |
| form | `form.<kind>.<scope>.<field>` | `form.required.node.label`, `form.enum.node.node_type`, `form.range.node.impact`, `form.pattern.edge.to`, `form.type.node.item` |
| integrity | `integrity.<rule>` | `integrity.duplicate-id`, `integrity.dangling-from`, `integrity.dangling-to`, `integrity.dangling-trigger`, `integrity.orphan-node` (MUST); `integrity.testimony-in-prod`, `integrity.verified-before-fact`, `integrity.untraced-decision`, `integrity.refutes-unreconciled`, and the five `integrity.criterion-*` and `integrity.measured-*` codes of v4.12 (SHOULD) |
| yaml | `yaml.<rule>` | `yaml.forbidden-key-on` (MUST), `yaml.unquoted-date` (SHOULD) |
| semantic | `semantic.<rule>` | `semantic.contradiction` (MUST); `semantic.supersedes-unreconciled`, `semantic.answered-question-open`, `semantic.decision-done-dev`, `semantic.stale-missing`, `semantic.stale-old`, `semantic.review-overdue`, `semantic.testimony-unmarked`, and the `semantic.domain-*` codes of the domain layer (SHOULD), only in `optional/` |

`<kind>` ∈ `required enum type pattern range const unknown-key exclusive`. `<scope>` ∈ `top meta node edge`.
In a nested object, `<field>` is the dotted path: `form.required.node.provenance.locator`.
`range` also covers text length: `label: ""` (MUST) and a `label` longer than 280 characters (SHOULD, because the
narrative goes in `narrative`). Length counts code points, like JSON Schema's `maxLength`: an emoji counts as 1, not
as 2 UTF-16 units (JavaScript's `str.length` would get it wrong), and there is no normalization.
A full date must exist on the calendar, and the code is `form.pattern`: the schema's `format: date` is an
**assertion**, and every reader must check it. `.nan` and `.inf` fail as `form.type` in any position, including under
an `x_` key and inside a list, because JSON cannot represent them. A list item that is not a mapping uses the `item`
field (`form.type.node.item`). A key name that is not a slug (`<<`, `1.0`, `a.b`) fails as `form.pattern.<scope>.key`;
with the `x_` prefix, it only warns. Keys are compared in their JSON form: `1` and `"1"` collide
(`parse.duplicate-key`), and `true` becomes `true`, not `True`. An edge with `on` fails with `yaml.forbidden-key-on`;
if the target of `on` does not exist, `integrity.dangling-on` comes out too. The `pattern` keywords follow ECMA-262
semantics, as in JSON Schema: `$` does not match before a final line break.

What v4 changed in severity, and what it added:

| Code | In v3 | In v4 |
|---|---|---|
| `form.required.node.provenance` (a `confirmed` or PROD node without `provenance`; `unverifiable` does not require it) | SHOULD | **MUST** |
| `form.unknown-key.<scope>.<key>` (a key outside the grammar and without `x_`, at the top level, in meta, in a node, or in an edge) | SHOULD | **MUST** |
| `form.pattern.<scope>.key` (a name that is not a slug, without `x_`) | SHOULD | **MUST** (with `x_`, still SHOULD) |
| `form.pattern.node.provenance.source` (a placeholder `source`: whitespace only, `desconhecida`, `unknown`, `n/a`, `none`, `null`, `sem fonte`, `tbd`, hyphens, an em dash, `?`...) | — | **MUST** (an empty value still gives `form.range`) |
| `form.pattern.node.provenance.method` (not in the form `'<class>: <detail>'`, with the class one of `medição` (measurement), `leitura` (reading), `juízes` (judges), `derivado` (derived), or `testemunho` (testimony)) | — | SHOULD (MUST in v5) |
| `form.unknown-key.node.provenance.<key>` (an unknown key inside `provenance`) | SHOULD | SHOULD |

v4.1 adds four SHOULD warnings (no verdict changes; `latest/form/unanchored/` and `latest/integrity/coherence/`).
The three `integrity.*` codes cross fields or edges, so the reader computes them outside the schema:

| Code | When it warns |
|---|---|
| `form.required.node.verified_against` | a `claim` with `verified_at` and without `verified_against`: a stamp with no target (the other node types already anchor themselves through another field) |
| `integrity.testimony-in-prod` | a PROD node whose basis is testimony (`evidence_class: testimony` or a `method` of class `testemunho`) |
| `integrity.verified-before-fact` | `verified_at` earlier than `valid_from`, compared at the granularity of the shorter one (`YYYY`, `YYYY-MM`, `YYYY-MM-DD`); a date outside these forms is not compared |
| `integrity.untraced-decision` | a `decision` that is neither `superseded` nor `refuted`, with no `trace`, no `provenance`, and no outgoing `TRACES_TO` edge |

v4.3 adds `external_edges`, optional, at the top level: edges between graphs with **exactly one** external end,
`<path relative to the repository root>#<id>`, while the other end is an id in this file or absent (an absent `from`
stands for the whole graph). The types are `SUPERSEDES`, `CONSTRAINS`, `SUPPORTS`, `REFUTES`, `TRACES_TO`, and
`DEPENDS_ON`. The cases live in `latest/form/external-edges/`, `latest/integrity/external-local/`, and
`latest/integrity/external-corpus/`.

| Code | When it fails |
|---|---|
| `form.pattern.top.external_edges.to` (or `.from`) | both ends external, both ends local, or a reference outside the form (an absolute path, or no `.kg.yaml#` or `.kg.json#`) |
| `form.enum.top.external_edges.edge_type` | a type outside the six (the domain-layer types do not cross graphs) |
| `integrity.dangling-external-local` | the local end does not exist in this file |
| `integrity.dangling-external` | **with the corpus**: the file or the id of the external end does not exist |

An external edge counts as a link: a node linked only by one is not an orphan. Without the corpus, the reader does
not check the external end, and it says so in its output. The reference is relative and uses `/`: segments start with
a letter, a digit, or `_`, with no `.` or `..` segments, no `\`, and no `:`.

**The `.kg.json` format.** The same data model can come as JSON, in a `.kg.json` file, read by a JSON parser under
the contract's **JSON profile** (`latest/json/`). In it, these points are **MUST**:

| Point | What fails | Code |
|---|---|---|
| Numbers per I-JSON (RFC 7493) | an integer-valued number with magnitude above 2^53−1, written as an integer or as a float (`9007199254740992`, `1e20`); a value that overflows a double (`1e400`, a 401-digit integer) is already non-finite | `form.type.<scope>.<field>`, the same path as `.nan` |
| Strings without a lone surrogate (I-JSON) | `\ud800` without its pair, in a key or a value; the pair `😀` is a single character | `parse.yaml-error` |
| Depth | more than 128 nested collections (the root counts as 1) | `parse.yaml-error` |
| RFC 8259 whitespace | only space, tab, LF, and CR; a leading BOM is accepted and dropped, and anything else fails (NBSP and `\x1c` are not whitespace) | `parse.yaml-error` |
| RFC 8259 syntax | a comment, a trailing comma, an unquoted key, single quotes, `NaN`, `Infinity` | `parse.yaml-error` |
| Unique keys (ADR 002) | the same key twice in an object, compared after escapes are resolved | `parse.duplicate-key` |

An empty document, one with only RFC whitespace, or `null` is `parse.empty-document`. Invalid JSON syntax uses
`parse.yaml-error`: the vocabulary has no `parse.json-error`. In `.kg.yaml`, the first three points are **SHOULD**, and
the YAML MUST verdict does not change (`latest/yaml/json-profile/`):

| Code | When it warns |
|---|---|
| `yaml.unsafe-integer` | an integer-valued number outside ±(2^53−1) |
| `yaml.lone-surrogate` | a lone surrogate in a key or a text value |
| `yaml.depth-over-128` | more than 128 nested collections (the YAML parse limit stays at 1000) |

v4.2 adds `provenance.locality`, optional, with the enum `repo`, `web`, `host`, or `pessoa`. A value outside the enum
warns as `form.enum.node.provenance.locality` (`latest/form/provenance-locality/`), and no verdict changes.

v4.4 adds `integrity.refutes-unreconciled` (`latest/integrity/coherence/`): a node that receives `REFUTES` and stays
alive, that is, neither `superseded` nor `refuted`. A `question` that is `done` does not warn, because it is already
answered. The graph asserts and refutes the same thing. In `optional/semantic/`, the same graph fails as
`semantic.contradiction`, which is what the radar does; in the contract the case is SHOULD for now, and it becomes
MUST in a future version, after adopters measure their own debt.

v4.4 also closes three rare YAML constructs where readers disagreed (`latest/yaml/strict-profile/`), taking the
strictest verdict in all three, by a contract decision of 2026-10-19. All of them fail as `parse.yaml-error`:
- the unnamed `!` tag, also in the form `!<!>`, on a scalar or a collection;
- an explicit `!!timestamp` whose text is not a date in the strict form: the intersection of PyYAML's constructor and
  the one in the JavaScript `yaml` package (two-digit minute and second, a fraction with at least one digit, a time
  zone up to ±29, and only a space between the date and the time);
- a tab outside quotes, a literal block, or a comment (as whitespace or inside an unquoted text value), as in PyYAML's
  pure parser.

Measured on 2026-10-20: none of the 1,391 `.kg.yaml` files in four adopter repositories changes its verdict.

v4.5 adds four things:
- `verified_scope`, optional, the reach of `verified_at` (`latest/form/verified-scope/`). The MUST level only accepts
  the key; at the SHOULD level, the enum is `fato`, `mecanismo`, or `nenhum` (a value outside it warns as
